transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thank you. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time letting go of worries once they start. It’s probably not the biggest thing, but it’s been wearing on me.

Like, I’ll worry about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report I need to finish, or whether I missed something at work, and then I just can’t seem to… shelve it, I suppose. I make lists, I try to redirect myself, but it keeps circling back anyway. Does that make sense?
Did these worries start after a particular stressful event or change in your life?

Yes… I think it did, in a way. It’s been about a year and two months now, since my mother moved into my home after she had a fall.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic—because we’ve managed, really—but that does seem to be when the worrying became harder to put down.
When these worries come up, do you feel driven to do anything over and over—like checking on your mother repeatedly—to relieve the anxiety?

I’m not sure I’d call it “driven,” exactly… I mean, I do sometimes feel like I should check something or make sure everything’s okay, but I don’t know that it’s over and over in that sense.

Maybe I’m not understanding the distinction. It’s more that the thought keeps bothering me, and I try to reassure myself, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying about many different parts of your life, not just your mother’s care?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, it started with my mother’s safety, but over this past year it’s sort of… spread out.

I worry about money, decisions with staff at work, deadlines, the house—whether I’ve forgotten something important. And then there’s this constant question of whether I’m being a good enough daughter, which I know probably isn’t very useful.

Even small things can start to feel like they’re going to unravel if I don’t keep on top of them. I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it, but yes, it’s not just about my mother anymore.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed?

Um… I don’t think I’d say depressed, exactly. Not in a major way. I’ve had some lower moments, I suppose, but I’ve mostly thought of it as stress or being worn out.

I’m not sure if that answers it properly. I haven’t really noticed feeling “down” as the main thing, if that makes sense.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control the worry?

Yes… I think that’s actually the hardest part. I try not to make too much of it, but once a worry starts, it’s very difficult for me to put it away.

It can be about my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or something at work I’m afraid I’ve missed. I’ll make lists, or try to redirect myself, and I can function, but it’s like my mind won’t shelve it properly. It keeps coming back even when I know I’ve already thought it through.

I’m not sure if that’s what you mean by “control,” but… yes, it does feel hard to stop.
Have you been feeling restless or on edge a lot lately?

I’m not completely sure. I wouldn’t have used the word “restless,” maybe… but I suppose I do feel keyed up sometimes, like I’m waiting for something to go wrong.

I can usually sit still and do what I need to do, so it’s not obvious, I don’t think. It’s more an internal sort of on-edge feeling. Does that count?
Do you often feel tense or unable to relax?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but by the end of the day my neck and shoulders can feel really tight, almost like I’ve been bracing myself without noticing.

And I do catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes, especially when I’m answering emails or listening for my mother in the next room. I suppose that’s tension, isn’t it?
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes… somewhat. I mean, I do sleep, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most nights I’m lying there for quite a while replaying the day or trying to think through what might go wrong tomorrow.

And if I wake up because I hear my mother moving around, then I’m usually just… awake. It can take an hour or two to settle back down, and then I go into the library feeling like I haven’t really rested. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
If your mother were no longer living with you, do you think the worrying would still be a problem?

I’d like to say it would all settle down if she weren’t living with me, because that would be a simpler answer… but I don’t think that’s completely true.

It started mostly around worrying about her safety, but over the past year it’s sort of spread. I find myself worrying about finances, decisions with staff at work, deadlines, the house… and whether I’m being a good daughter. Even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that properly, but yes, I think the worrying would probably still be there.
Do these thoughts ever feel intrusive and unwanted, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yes… I think that’s a fair way to put it. I don’t mean they’re bizarre thoughts or anything, it’s more that once a worry gets going, I can’t seem to put it away.

Like if I start thinking about my mother getting up in the night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work, it just keeps coming back even when I’m trying to focus on something else. I make lists, I check things, I tell myself I’ve done what I can… but it’s as if I can’t shelve it in my mind. Is that what you mean by intrusive?
When you check on something, do you feel you have to do it again and again before the anxiety eases?

Not really in that sense, I don’t think. I might check once to reassure myself, or maybe look back at something if I’m still uneasy, but it’s not like I have to do it over and over until it feels “right.”

At least… I don’t think so. It’s more that the worry keeps hanging around afterward, even if I’ve checked. Does that distinction make sense?
Has this worrying been interfering with your work or your ability to manage things at home?

A bit, yes… I mean, I’m still getting things done, mostly, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But it has started to show up at work.

I’ve missed some small but important details at the library, which really isn’t like me. And there was a grant presentation where I just… froze, and I had to hand off parts of it to someone else. I was embarrassed by that.

At home I’m managing, but it feels harder than it should. And at work, I’ve started worrying that maybe I’m not leading my team as well as I should be. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you feel your anxiety is mainly tied to caring for your mother?

At first I would have said yes, mostly. My mother’s safety was the thing I could point to, and that felt… understandable, I suppose.

But if I’m honest, over this past year it’s spread beyond that. I worry about finances, decisions with staff, deadlines, things around the house, whether I’m being a good daughter… and then even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that clearly. It’s not only my mother anymore, even though she’s still a big part of it.
Do you feel your level of worry is more than the situation with your mother reasonably calls for?

Yes… I think so. I don’t love saying that, because of course my mother’s situation is real, and I don’t want to seem like I’m overreacting.

But honestly, over the past year it’s gone beyond just worrying about her safety. I find myself worrying about finances, staff decisions, deadlines, things around the house, whether I’m being a good daughter… and then even small things can feel like they’re about to unravel.

So yes, I suppose the level of worry is probably more than the situation itself calls for. Does that make sense?
Do you think your anxiety is still mostly a reaction to your mother moving in after her fall?

I think it started that way, yes. Her fall and moving in with me gave me something very real to focus on, and I don’t want to minimize that.

But… no, I don’t think it’s only that anymore. Over the past year, the worry has sort of spread. I’ll worry about finances, staff decisions, deadlines, things at home, whether I’m being a good daughter… and then even small things can start to feel like they’re about to unravel.

So I suppose it’s still connected to my mother, but not just a reaction to her moving in. Does that make sense?
